title: Enterprise Virtualization: KVM & Proxmox VE
subtitle: Design, run and protect a highly available virtualization cluster
audience_line: System administrators who run or plan a virtualization platform
overview: This programme teaches participants to build and run a virtualization platform on open-source software. They start with KVM, QEMU and libvirt on a single host, then deploy Proxmox VE: networking with bridges, VLANs, bonds and SDN, local and shared storage up to hyperconverged Ceph, virtual machines and LXC containers, automation through the API and Ansible, clustering with high availability and live migration, access control, firewalling and backups with Proxmox Backup Server. They also migrate virtual machines from VMware ESXi and compare the platforms on the market. Every chapter ends with a lab, and the programme closes with a final project in which teams deploy and present a three-node cluster.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: System administrators who run or plan a virtualization platform

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Linux administration (course: Linux & Bash Scripting, or RHCSA Part 1: Red Hat System Administration I) and basic IP networking. Linux basics are not taught again

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 36 h: 30 h of chapters + 6 h buffer, in 12 sessions of 3 h

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs on premises: one lab server per team of two or three (64 GB RAM, nested virtualization), provided by the organiser, hosting as virtual machines a KVM host, three Proxmox VE nodes, a Proxmox Backup Server and a source hypervisor for migration; Windows evaluation images; no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can deploy and operate a Proxmox VE cluster with shared storage, high availability, tested backups and migrated workloads, and choose a platform for their organisation

phases.name: KVM & Proxmox VE Foundations
phases.focus: KVM and libvirt, Proxmox VE networking and storage
phases.intro: Participants see how a hypervisor works with KVM, QEMU and libvirt on a single host, then install Proxmox VE and build the networking and storage it needs: Linux bridges, VLANs, bonds and SDN, local LVM-thin and ZFS, shared NFS and iSCSI, and hyperconverged Ceph. Ceph is introduced here and deployed in phase 3, once the cluster exists. Validated lab: a Proxmox VE node with a VLAN-aware bridge, ZFS local storage and an NFS share, managed from the web interface and the command line.

chapters.title: Virtualization & KVM
chapters.content: Hypervisor types, KVM and QEMU, libvirt, virsh, virt-install, Cockpit

chapters.title: Proxmox VE Architecture
chapters.content: Installation, web interface and command line, nodes, Linux bridges, VLANs and bonds, SDN

chapters.title: Storage
chapters.content: Local LVM-thin and ZFS, NFS and iSCSI shared storage, hyperconverged Ceph

phases.name: Virtual Machines & Containers
phases.focus: VMs, templates and cloud-init, LXC containers and automation
phases.intro: Participants create Linux and Windows virtual machines with VirtIO drivers, turn them into cloud-init templates, and use snapshots and clones. They run LXC containers, then automate the platform through its API, pvesh and Ansible. Validated lab: a cloud-init template cloned into three configured virtual machines by an Ansible playbook.

chapters.title: Virtual Machines
chapters.content: Linux and Windows VMs, VirtIO drivers, cloud-init, templates, snapshots, clones

chapters.title: Containers & Automation
chapters.content: LXC containers, the Proxmox VE API and pvesh, automation with Ansible

phases.name: Clustering, Operations & Migration
phases.focus: High availability, access control, backups, migration, platform choice
phases.intro: Participants join nodes into a cluster with quorum, move running machines with live migration and protect them with high availability. They control access, firewall the platform, back up and restore with Proxmox Backup Server, migrate workloads from VMware ESXi and other hypervisors, and compare Proxmox VE with the alternatives now that Red Hat Virtualization has reached end of life. Validated lab: a virtual machine on Ceph storage restarted automatically on another node after a node failure, then restored from backup.

chapters.title: Clustering & High Availability
chapters.content: Corosync cluster, quorum and QDevice, live migration, HA rules (node and resource affinity), fencing

chapters.title: Operations & Security
chapters.content: Users, roles and realms (LDAP and Active Directory), permissions, firewall, updates, Proxmox Backup Server, restore

chapters.title: Migrating to Proxmox VE
chapters.content: ESXi import wizard, virt-v2v, OVF and OVA import, migration planning

chapters.title: The Enterprise Landscape
chapters.content: Red Hat Virtualization end of life, oVirt as a community project, OpenShift Virtualization (KubeVirt), choosing a platform

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A three-node highly available cluster, presented to the group
phases.intro: Teams of two or three design and deploy a three-node Proxmox VE cluster on their lab server, reusing the phase labs, then present it as they would to an IT manager choosing a platform.

chapters.title: Design & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, design the network and storage, then build the three-node cluster with Ceph or shared storage, templates and an HA virtual machine

chapters.title: Migrate, Back Up & Document
chapters.content: Migrate a virtual machine from another hypervisor, run and restore a backup, write the architecture diagram and runbook

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live migration and a node failure during the demo; questions and feedback

project.title: A Highly Available Virtualization Cluster
project.brief: A three-node Proxmox VE cluster with Ceph or shared storage, templates, a highly available virtual machine that survives a node failure, live migration, a tested backup and restore plan, and a virtual machine migrated from another hypervisor.
project.stack: Proxmox VE, KVM, QEMU, LXC, Ceph or NFS, ZFS, Corosync, Proxmox Backup Server, cloud-init, Ansible
project.deliverable: Working cluster, architecture diagram, backup plan and runbook, live demo
